- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ["main"]
  pull_request:
    branches: ["main"]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  MISE_GITHUB_GITHUB_ATTESTATIONS: false
  # Read by Apps/Tuist.swift at generation. Off for every job by default — with the
  # COMPILATION_CACHE_* settings baked in but no cache service, each compile task
  # waits out a CAS socket deadline. app-build flips it on once its service is up.
  TUIST_CACHE_ENABLED: "false"

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: macos-15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: jdx/mise-action@v4
        with:
          experimental: true
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Check formatting (Swift + Markdown)
        run: mise run format-check

      - name: Lint (SwiftLint + actionlint)
        run: mise run lint

  build-test:
    name: Build & Test (macOS)
    runs-on: macos-15
    needs: lint
    env:
      DEVELOPER_DIR: "/Applications/Xcode_26.2.app/Contents/Developer"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Swift 6.3 toolchain
        run: |
          curl -fLo swift-6.3.pkg "https://download.swift.org/swift-6.3-release/xcode/swift-6.3-RELEASE/swift-6.3-RELEASE-osx.pkg"
          sudo installer -pkg swift-6.3.pkg -target /
          TOOLCHAINS=$(plutil -extract CFBundleIdentifier raw /Library/Developer/Toolchains/swift-6.3-RELEASE.xctoolchain/Info.plist)
          echo "TOOLCHAINS=$TOOLCHAINS" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Cache SPM dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: .build
          # Keyed on the workspace path: .build/workspace-state.json records the WebRTC
          # xcframework absolutely, so a cache restored elsewhere (as after the repo
          # rename) sends SwiftPM looking where the artifact is not.
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-swift-6.3-spm-${{ github.workspace }}-${{ hashFiles('Package.swift', 'Package.resolved') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-swift-6.3-spm-${{ github.workspace }}-

      - uses: jdx/mise-action@v4
        with:
          experimental: true
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Show Swift version
        run: swift --version

      # Through the mise task, not a copy of its commands: GitHub runs `run:` under
      # `bash -e` without pipefail, so a piped `swift build … | xcsift` reports
      # xcsift's exit 0 and a failed build lands as a green job.
      - name: Build & test
        run: mise run test

  # `swift build` never reaches Apps/ReachyMini — it is an Xcode target, not an SPM
  # one, so nothing but SwiftLint ever looked at it. This job is the only thing that
  # compiles the app shell and the Tuist manifest that generates it.
  app-build:
    name: App Build (ReachyMini, macOS + iOS)
    runs-on: macos-15
    needs: lint
    timeout-minutes: 60
    # `id-token` is what lets the step below authenticate over OIDC instead of a stored token.
    # Job-level permissions replace the defaults wholesale, hence the explicit `contents: read`
    # for checkout.
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
    env:
      DEVELOPER_DIR: "/Applications/Xcode_26.2.app/Contents/Developer"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Deliberately Xcode's own Swift, with no swift.org toolchain overlaid:
      # xcodebuild cannot load the local package's manifest under one (its clang
      # fails to spawn the linker). This job exists to compile the app shell and the
      # Tuist manifest; build-test is what holds the code to Swift 6.3.
      - uses: jdx/mise-action@v4
        with:
          experimental: true
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Build insights reach tuist.dev through the `tuist inspect build` post-action Tuist
      # writes into every generated scheme, and that post-action needs a session. OIDC mints a
      # short-lived one with no stored secret, but only for a branch of this repository: a
      # fork's workflow gets no id-token, so the step is skipped there. It also needs the
      # repository connected to the server project, without which the server answers "No
      # projects linked to the repository" — a warning rather than a red build, since this job
      # exists to compile the app shell and the widget, not to carry telemetry. Generation
      # itself needs none of it: Apps/Tuist.swift sets optionalAuthentication.
      - name: Authenticate with tuist.dev (OIDC)
        if: ${{ !github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork }}
        working-directory: Apps
        run: mise x -- tuist auth login || echo "::warning::No tuist.dev session — this run's build insights go unrecorded."

      # The compilation cache answers only through the service `tuist setup cache`
      # starts, so the env flips to true strictly after its socket is live — settings
      # baked in with no service behind them stall every compile task instead (the
      # workflow-level default covers forks, which have no session to set it up with).
      - name: Set up Tuist cache
        if: ${{ !github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork }}
        working-directory: Apps
        run: |
          mise x -- tuist setup cache || true
          SOCK="$HOME/.local/state/tuist/alexey1312_reachy-mini-swift.sock"
          for _ in $(seq 1 10); do [ -S "$SOCK" ] && break; sleep 1; done
          if [ -S "$SOCK" ]; then
            echo "TUIST_CACHE_ENABLED=true" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          else
            echo "::warning::Tuist cache service did not start — building uncached."
          fi

      # `build:app` generates the project first (depends = ["project"]).
      - name: Build ReachyMini
        run: mise run build:app

      # The macOS destination leaves ReachyWidget out entirely (iOS-only extension,
      # embedded under `condition: .when([.ios])`), so until this step the widget's
      # sources were compiled by nothing at all.
      - name: Build ReachyMini + widget (iOS)
        run: mise run build:app:ios

      # Release guards archive-ability: nothing else compiles this configuration,
      # so without these steps a broken Release first surfaces at archive time.
      - name: Build ReachyMini (macOS, Release)
        run: mise run build:app:release

      - name: Build ReachyMini + widget (iOS, Release)
        run: mise run build:app:ios:release

  # The one job that launches the app binary: XCUITest walks the connect gate on
  # a simulator. Tier 2 (the sim-daemon path) needs the MuJoCo venv and stays local.
  smoke:
    name: Smoke (iOS Simulator)
    runs-on: macos-15
    needs: lint
    timeout-minutes: 60
    env:
      DEVELOPER_DIR: "/Applications/Xcode_26.2.app/Contents/Developer"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: jdx/mise-action@v4
        with:
          experimental: true
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Smoke test
        run: mise run test:smoke

#!/bin/sh
# =============================================================================
# ReachyMini development environment bootstrap
# =============================================================================
# The single entry point for setting up this repo after cloning. Idempotent.
# Installs all pinned tools via the self-contained ./bin/mise and wires git
# hooks. No global mise, brew, or manual tool installs required.
#
# Swift itself is managed by swiftly (https://www.swift.org/swiftly/) via the
# .swift-version file — install swiftly separately if `swift --version`
# doesn't match .swift-version.
# =============================================================================
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

echo "==> Trusting mise config"
./bin/mise trust --yes mise.toml

echo "==> Installing pinned tools (swiftformat, swiftlint, hk, dprint, tuist, ...)"
./bin/mise install

echo "==> Wiring git hooks (.githooks via core.hooksPath)"
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
chmod +x .githooks/*

# Snapshot reference images are LFS pointers; without the filter they check out as text stubs
# and every snapshot test fails with an unreadable-image error.
echo "==> Enabling Git LFS for this clone"
# LFS hooks are tracked in .githooks and combined with hk where necessary.
# Install only the local filters so git-lfs does not reject those existing hooks.
./bin/mise x -- git lfs install --local --skip-repo

# Apps/Tuist.swift enables the Xcode compilation cache by default, and the cache
# only answers through this per-user LaunchAgent — without it every compile task
# waits out a CAS socket deadline. Needs a tuist.dev session, hence best-effort.
echo "==> Setting up the Tuist Xcode cache service (LaunchAgent)"
TUIST="$(./bin/mise where tuist)/tuist"
(cd Apps && env -u TOOLCHAINS "$TUIST" setup cache) || {
  echo "WARNING: tuist setup cache failed — no tuist.dev session?"
  echo "         Run './bin/mise x -- tuist auth login' and re-run bootstrap,"
  echo "         or generate with TUIST_CACHE_ENABLED=false to build uncached."
}

echo "==> Done"
./bin/mise run setup
echo ""
echo "Next steps:"
echo "  ./bin/mise run build   # build the Swift package"
echo "  ./bin/mise run test    # run tests"
echo "  ./bin/mise tasks       # list all tasks"

18	enter = """
19	git config core.hooksPath .githooks 2>/dev/null || true
20	"""

23	# --- Swift Development ---

31	dprint = "0.55.2" # Markdown formatting

33	# --- Snapshots & Storybook ---
34	# The release ships a single lowercase `prefire` binary, which the backend cannot guess from the
35	# repository name — hence the explicit exe option.
36	"github:BarredEwe/Prefire[exe=prefire]" = "5.7.0"

41	actionlint = "1.7.12" # GitHub Actions linting

49	description = "Build the Swift package (debug)"

51	set -o pipefail

53	"""

55	[tasks."build:release"]
56	description = "Build the Swift package (release)"
57	run = """
58	set -o pipefail
59	swift build --configuration release 2>&1 | xcsift
60	"""
61	
62	# `build` and `test` are SwiftPM only — Apps/ReachyMini is an Xcode target and
63	# nothing else compiles it. Signing is off: the runner has no team, and the
64	# personal one lives in CLAUDE.local.md.
65	[tasks."build:app"]
66	description = "Build the ReachyMini app target (macOS)"

69	# `tuist inspect build` post-action into every generated scheme, and it reads the

100	  -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
101	  -resultBundlePath "$RESULT_BUNDLE" \

103	  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \

108	# Release configuration, so a broken one would first surface at archive time.
109	[tasks."build:app:release"]
110	description = "Build the ReachyMini app target (macOS, Release, unsigned)"
111	depends = ["project"]

113	set -o pipefail
114	RESULT_BUNDLE=Apps/DerivedData/ResultBundles/ReachyMini-macOS-release.xcresult
115	rm -rf "$RESULT_BUNDLE"
116	xcodebuild -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachyMini \
117	  -destination 'platform=macOS' -configuration Release \
118	  -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
119	  -resultBundlePath "$RESULT_BUNDLE" \
120	  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
121	  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
122	  build 2>&1 | xcsift
123	'''

127	depends = ["project"]

136	  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
137	  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \

142	description = "Build, install and launch on a connected iPhone (see Scripts/device-run.sh)"
143	depends = ["project"]
144	run = "./Scripts/device-run.sh"

148	depends = ["project"]

180	set -o pipefail
181	SIM="${REACHY_SMOKE_SIM:-iPhone 17 Pro}"
182	xcrun simctl boot "$SIM" 2>/dev/null || true
183	xcodebuild test -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachyMini \
184	  -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,name=${SIM}" \
185	  -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
186	  -testLanguage en -testRegion US \
187	  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
188	  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
189	  2>&1 | xcsift
190	'''
191	
192	[tasks."test:smoke:sim"]
193	description = "Smoke the whole user path against a running sim daemon (start with: mise run sim-daemon)"
194	depends = ["project"]
195	run = '''
196	set -o pipefail
197	SIM="${REACHY_SMOKE_SIM:-iPhone 17 Pro}"
198	xcrun simctl boot "$SIM" 2>/dev/null || true
199	# TEST_RUNNER_ forwards the variable into the XCUITest runner's environment.
200	xcodebuild test -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachyMini \
201	  -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,name=${SIM}" \
202	  -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
203	  -testLanguage en -testRegion US \
204	  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
205	  TEST_RUNNER_REACHY_SMOKE_HOST="${REACHY_SMOKE_HOST:-127.0.0.1:8000}" \

212	run = """
213	set -o pipefail

215	"""

217	# Snapshots run on an iOS simulator, so they live in Apps/ as an Xcode target and never reach
218	# `swift test`. Both the device and the OS are pinned: a different runtime renders text
219	# differently and every reference would have to be re-recorded.
220	[tasks."snapshots:_run"]
221	hide = true
222	depends = ["project"]
223	run = '''
224	set -o pipefail
225	SIM="${REACHY_SNAPSHOT_SIM:-iPhone 17 Pro}"
226	# Belt and braces since the forked template took over: each preview is captured in both
227	# appearances from an injected trait, and the surfaces gallery re-recorded on a *dark* simulator
228	# came out byte-identical, so the trait decides. Left here for whatever the trait does not reach.
229	xcrun simctl boot "$SIM" 2>/dev/null || true
230	xcrun simctl ui "$SIM" appearance light >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
231	# References are English-only on purpose. Every string this app shows is localizable, and a
232	# simulator left in another language would re-render all 1000 of them in it.
233	xcodebuild test -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachyUISnapshotTests \
234	  -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,name=${SIM},OS=${REACHY_SNAPSHOT_OS:-26.4.1}" \
235	  -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
236	  -testLanguage en -testRegion US \
237	  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
238	  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
239	  2>&1 | xcsift
240	'''
241	
242	[tasks."test:snapshots"]
243	description = "Snapshot-test every ReachyUI preview (fails if a reference had to be recorded)"
244	run = '''
245	#!/bin/bash
246	set -euo pipefail
247	DIR=Apps/ReachyUISnapshotTests/__Snapshots__
248	# Prefire generates `record: .missing`, so an absent reference is written rather than compared.
249	# Comparing the images either side of the run reports that as a failure even if the suite itself
250	# is happy — a reference that had to be written verified nothing. Checksums rather than
251	# `git status`, so an uncommitted tree does not read as a failure.
252	fingerprint() { find "$DIR" -name '*.png' -exec shasum -a 256 {} + 2>/dev/null | sort; }
253	BEFORE="$(fingerprint)"
254	./bin/mise run snapshots:_run
255	AFTER="$(fingerprint)"
256	if [ "$BEFORE" != "$AFTER" ]; then
257	  echo "Snapshot references were written during the run, so they verified nothing:" >&2
258	  diff <(echo "$BEFORE") <(echo "$AFTER") >&2 || true
259	  echo "Review the images, or re-record them all with: mise run test:snapshots:record" >&2
260	  exit 1
261	fi
262	'''
263	
264	[tasks."test:snapshots:record"]
265	description = "Delete and re-record every snapshot reference, leaving the diff for review"
266	run = '''
267	#!/bin/bash
268	set -euo pipefail
269	DIR=Apps/ReachyUISnapshotTests/__Snapshots__
270	# `record: .missing` only writes absent references, so re-recording means removing them first.
271	[ -d "$DIR" ] && find "$DIR" -name '*.png' -delete
272	# swift-snapshot-testing reports a freshly recorded reference as a test failure, which is the
273	# expected outcome here — the point of this task is to write them.
274	./bin/mise run snapshots:_run || true
275	git status --short -- "$DIR"
276	'''
277	
278	[tasks.storybook]
279	description = "Regenerate the preview catalogue and run the storybook app on a simulator"
280	run = '''
281	#!/bin/bash
282	set -euo pipefail
283	SIM="${REACHY_SNAPSHOT_SIM:-iPhone 17 Pro}"
284	# The playbook plugin only ever scans its own target's sources, so the CLI is driven directly.
285	prefire playbook Sources/ReachyDesign/Previews Sources/ReachyUI/Previews Apps/ReachyMini/Previews \
286	  --output Apps/ReachyStorybook/Generated \
287	  --config Apps
288	./bin/mise run project
289	set -o pipefail
290	xcodebuild -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachyStorybook \
291	  -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,name=$SIM,OS=${REACHY_SNAPSHOT_OS:-26.4.1}" \
292	  -configuration Debug -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
293	  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
294	  build 2>&1 | xcsift
295	xcrun simctl boot "$SIM" 2>/dev/null || true
296	open -a Simulator
297	xcrun simctl install "$SIM" Apps/DerivedData/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/ReachyStorybook.app
298	xcrun simctl launch "$SIM" com.alexey1312.ReachyMiniStorybook
299	'''
300	
301	[tasks.lint]
302	description = "Run SwiftLint, actionlint, and the hk version lockstep check"
303	run = '''
304	set -o pipefail
305	PINNED="$(sed -nE 's/^hk = "([0-9.]+)".*/\1/p' mise.toml)"
306	DRIFT="$(grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' hk.pkl | sort -u | grep -vFx "$PINNED" || true)"
307	if [ -n "$DRIFT" ]; then
308	  echo "hk.pkl references $DRIFT but mise.toml pins $PINNED — bump both together." >&2
309	  exit 1
310	fi
311	swiftlint lint --strict Sources Tests Apps/ReachyMini Apps/ReachyMiniUITests Apps/ReachyStorybook Apps/ReachyUISnapshotTests 2>&1 | xcsift
312	actionlint

# =============================================================================
# mise Configuration for ReachyMini
# =============================================================================
# Bootstrap: run ./bootstrap.sh once after cloning. No global mise needed —
# ./bin/mise is a self-contained bootstrap binary (mise generate bootstrap).
#
# To update the embedded mise version:
#   mise generate bootstrap > ./bin/mise && chmod +x ./bin/mise
# =============================================================================

[settings]
experimental = true
legacy_version_file = false

# Safety net for developers who skipped ./bootstrap.sh: wire git hooks on
# directory entry via the native core.hooksPath mechanism.
[hooks]
enter = """
git config core.hooksPath .githooks 2>/dev/null || true
"""

[tools]
# --- Swift Development ---
# Swift itself is managed by swiftly via .swift-version, not by mise.
swiftformat = "0.62.1" # Swift code formatting
swiftlint = "0.65.0"   # Swift linting
xcsift = "1.3.1"       # xcodebuild/swift output filtering
tuist = "4.203.1"      # Xcode project generation (Apps/)

# --- Documentation & Formatting ---
dprint = "0.55.2" # Markdown formatting

# --- Snapshots & Storybook ---
# The release ships a single lowercase `prefire` binary, which the backend cannot guess from the
# repository name — hence the explicit exe option.
"github:BarredEwe/Prefire[exe=prefire]" = "5.7.0"
git-lfs = "3.7.1" # Snapshot reference images

# --- Git & CI ---
hk = "1.54.0"         # Git hooks manager (version must match hk.pkl package URI)
actionlint = "1.7.12" # GitHub Actions linting
git-cliff = "2.13.1"  # Changelog generation

# --- Simulator ---
python = "3.12" # for sim-daemon venv: mujoco ships no wheels for newer pythons
uv = "0.12.1"   # installs into that venv as APFS clones — see sim-daemon

[tasks.build]
description = "Build the Swift package (debug)"
run = """
set -o pipefail
swift build 2>&1 | xcsift
"""

[tasks."build:release"]
description = "Build the Swift package (release)"
run = """
set -o pipefail
swift build --configuration release 2>&1 | xcsift
"""

# `build` and `test` are SwiftPM only — Apps/ReachyMini is an Xcode target and
# nothing else compiles it. Signing is off: the runner has no team, and the
# personal one lives in CLAUDE.local.md.
[tasks."build:app"]
description = "Build the ReachyMini app target (macOS)"
depends = ["project"]
# `-resultBundlePath` is what makes build insights reach tuist.dev. Tuist writes a
# `tuist inspect build` post-action into every generated scheme, and it reads the
# .xcactivitylog that xcodebuild only writes when a result bundle is requested — Xcode.app
# writes one unconditionally, which is why local Xcode builds were the only ones ever
# recorded. Without the flag the post-action fails with "couldn't find the most recent
# activity log" and, being a post-action, leaves the build green.
run = '''
set -o pipefail
RESULT_BUNDLE=Apps/DerivedData/ResultBundles/ReachyMini-macOS.xcresult
rm -rf "$RESULT_BUNDLE"
xcodebuild -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachyMini \
  -destination 'platform=macOS' -configuration Debug \
  -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
  -resultBundlePath "$RESULT_BUNDLE" \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
  build 2>&1 | xcsift
'''

# Project.swift embeds it with `condition: .when([.ios])`, so under `platform=macOS`
# it is not built at all. `generic/platform=iOS` compiles it without needing a
# device, a simulator or a signing identity.

description = "Build the ReachyMini app and its widget extension (iOS, unsigned)"
depends = ["project"]
run = '''
set -o pipefail
RESULT_BUNDLE=Apps/DerivedData/ResultBundles/ReachyMini-iOS.xcresult
rm -rf "$RESULT_BUNDLE"
xcodebuild -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachyMini \
  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' -configuration Debug \
  -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
  -resultBundlePath "$RESULT_BUNDLE" \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
  build 2>&1 | xcsift
'''

# Release configuration, so a broken one would first surface at archive time.

description = "Build the ReachyMini app target (macOS, Release, unsigned)"
depends = ["project"]
run = '''
set -o pipefail
RESULT_BUNDLE=Apps/DerivedData/ResultBundles/ReachyMini-macOS-release.xcresult
rm -rf "$RESULT_BUNDLE"
xcodebuild -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachyMini \
  -destination 'platform=macOS' -configuration Release \
  -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
  -resultBundlePath "$RESULT_BUNDLE" \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
  build 2>&1 | xcsift
'''

[tasks."build:app:ios:release"]
description = "Build the ReachyMini app and widget (iOS, Release, unsigned)"
depends = ["project"]
run = '''
set -o pipefail
RESULT_BUNDLE=Apps/DerivedData/ResultBundles/ReachyMini-iOS-release.xcresult
rm -rf "$RESULT_BUNDLE"
xcodebuild -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachyMini \
  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' -configuration Release \
  -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
  -resultBundlePath "$RESULT_BUNDLE" \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
  build 2>&1 | xcsift

  -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,name=${SIM}" \
  -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \

  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
  2>&1 | xcsift

description = "Integration tests against a running sim daemon (start with: mise run sim-daemon)"
run = """
set -o pipefail
REACHY_SIM_HOST=127.0.0.1 swift test --parallel --filter SimulatorIntegrationTests 2>&1 | xcsift
"""

# Snapshots run on an iOS simulator, so they live in Apps/ as an Xcode target and never reach
# `swift test`. Both the device and the OS are pinned: a different runtime renders text
# differently and every reference would have to be re-recorded.
[tasks."snapshots:_run"]
hide = true
depends = ["project"]
run = '''
set -o pipefail
SIM="${REACHY_SNAPSHOT_SIM:-iPhone 17 Pro}"
# Belt and braces since the forked template took over: each preview is captured in both
# appearances from an injected trait, and the surfaces gallery re-recorded on a *dark* simulator
# came out byte-identical, so the trait decides. Left here for whatever the trait does not reach.
xcrun simctl boot "$SIM" 2>/dev/null || true
xcrun simctl ui "$SIM" appearance light >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
# References are English-only on purpose. Every string this app shows is localizable, and a
# simulator left in another language would re-render all 1000 of them in it.
xcodebuild test -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachyUISnapshotTests \
  -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,name=${SIM},OS=${REACHY_SNAPSHOT_OS:-26.4.1}" \
  -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
  -testLanguage en -testRegion US \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
  2>&1 | xcsift
'''

[tasks."test:snapshots"]
description = "Snapshot-test every ReachyUI preview (fails if a reference had to be recorded)"
run = '''
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
DIR=Apps/ReachyUISnapshotTests/__Snapshots__
# Prefire generates `record: .missing`, so an absent reference is written rather than compared.
# Comparing the images either side of the run reports that as a failure even if the suite itself
# is happy — a reference that had to be written verified nothing. Checksums rather than
# `git status`, so an uncommitted tree does not read as a failure.
fingerprint() { find "$DIR" -name '*.png' -exec shasum -a 256 {} + 2>/dev/null | sort; }
BEFORE="$(fingerprint)"
./bin/mise run snapshots:_run
AFTER="$(fingerprint)"
if [ "$BEFORE" != "$AFTER" ]; then
  echo "Snapshot references were written during the run, so they verified nothing:" >&2
  diff <(echo "$BEFORE") <(echo "$AFTER") >&2 || true
  echo "Review the images, or re-record them all with: mise run test:snapshots:record" >&2
  exit 1
fi
'''

description = "Delete and re-record every snapshot reference, leaving the diff for review"

#!/bin/bash
